title: STAR-voting-library tabulation result
description: The machine-readable result of counting ONE election file with ONE method. Emitted by `starvote_larry_hastings.py <file> --json`. An implementation conforms on a case when its result validates against this schema and agrees with the reference result on `result.winners` and on every `rounds` value the method actually uses. Prose contract, versioning policy and worked examples: 07_Concepts/tabulation_engines/result_schema.md

schema_version.description: Version of THIS contract, not of any engine. patch = wording; minor = field added (old readers keep working); major = field removed or re-meant.

file.description: Basename of the election file counted.

sha256.description: Hash of the exact bytes counted. Two results are comparable only if this matches — it is what stops a stale fixture from being read as a disagreement.

declared_method.description: Verbatim `voting_method:` from the file, before alias resolution. null when the file declared none (the engine then defaults to STAR, or to RCV-IRV for ranked ballots).

method.description: The declared method normalized (lowercased, hyphens and spaces to underscores). Alias table: classify_method() in starvote_larry_hastings.py.

family.description: Which count ran. Determines which `rounds` keys are present.

candidates.description: In ballot order (the header row's left-to-right sequence, or first appearance on ranked ballots). This order IS the default tie-break priority when no lot order is published.

ballots_cast.description: Ballots after weight expansion — a `12 × 5,0,3` row is twelve ballots, not one.

max_score.description: Score ceiling for score ballots (5 in this library — a teaching guardrail, not an engine limit). null for methods with no score scale.

lot_order.description: The published tie-breaking lot, when the file pins one. null means ballot order was used.

winners.description: In the order elected. For a single-winner method, exactly one.

expected_winners.description: The file's own answer key, if it carries one. Not an output of the count — it is what the count is checked against.

matches_expected.description: null when there is no answer key. 'We did not check' and 'we checked and it failed' must not look alike.

rounds.description: The count itself. Which keys appear is fixed by election.family: score -> scoring (+ finalists/runoff for single-winner STAR); approval -> approval, abstentions; plurality -> votes, variant, votes_per_voter; ranked_robin -> record, smith_set; irv/stv -> irv_rounds, elimination_order (+ quota for STV).

finalists.description: The two candidates the Automatic Runoff actually used — which is NOT always the top two by score; see tiebreaks.

equal_support.description: Ballots scoring the two finalists equally: no preference between them. Excluded from the denominator.

majority.description: Strict majority OF THE DECIDED VOTERS (decided // 2 + 1) — the denominator the report prints. Not a majority of ballots cast.

variant.description: Which multi-member plurality this is (SNTV / Block / Limited). The tally is top-N by marks in every case; only the ballot differs.

overvotes.description: Single-winner Choose-One only: ballots marking more than one candidate, which count for nobody.

copeland.description: wins + 0.5 * draws — the academic tally, and what BetterVoting and pref_voting both score. Ranking on raw wins instead is the one convention that disagrees.

smith_set.description: Smallest group whose every member beats everyone outside it. Descriptive for Ranked Robin (Smith-efficient); a genuine pass/fail for IRV.

exhausted.description: Ballots that have stopped counting: cast minus still active. The number a round table never prints, and the one an IRV 'majority' has to be reconciled against.

elimination_order.description: Read back from the count, never recomputed — a recomputed order can contradict the rounds above it when a tie was settled by the second-choices ladder.

quota.description: STV only. Two published Droop rules exist and they differ by one vote; name which one produced the count.

tiebreaks.description: Every point where the ballots alone did not decide. EMPTY is a real claim: it says nothing was broken by a rung. This is the field that makes a right-winner-wrong-path result detectable.

rung.description: Which rung resolved it. Free text because the ladders differ per method AND per engine — LH breaks a Copeland tie by total margin then lot, BetterVoting by head-to-head. That divergence is data, not an error.

round.description: The selection round the tie happened in, for the methods that fill one seat per round (Bloc STAR, allocated, sss, rrv). Absent when the method has only one round, so a single-winner result carries no such key. Added in 1.1.0.

pairwise.description: Full head-to-head matrix. Part of the count for Ranked Robin; informational for the others, but it is what a conformance run needs to check Condorcet and Smith claims about a result.

prefer.description: prefer[A][B] = how row A fares against column B.

tally.description: One row per candidate, descending by value, ties in ballot order.
